questions.question_text:
An asset costs $\$52\,000$.
Straight-line depreciation removes $\$6500$ per year; declining-balance depreciation is $16\%$ p.a.
What is the **lower** of the two salvage values after $3$ years, to the nearest cent?

options.why: Chose the straight-line value, but the declining-balance value is lower after $3$ years.

questions.question_text:
A $\$15\,000$ asset can be depreciated by $\$1900$ per year (straight-line) or at $14\%$ p.a. (declining balance).
What is the **total depreciation** after $4$ years under the declining-balance method, to the nearest cent?

options.why: Gave the salvage value $15\,000(0.86)^{4}$ instead of the value lost.
Gave the straight-line total $1900 \times 4$ rather than the declining-balance total.
Took $14\%$ of the purchase price four times, instead of $14\%$ of the current value each year.

questions.question_text:
An asset costing $\$20\,000$ is depreciated either by $\$3200$ per year (straight-line) or at $24\%$ p.a. (declining balance).
What is the lower salvage value after $5$ years?

options.why: Chose the declining-balance value $20\,000(0.76)^{5}$, which is higher.
Subtracted only one year's straight-line depreciation: $20\,000 - 3200$.

questions.solution_text:
Straight-line:
$S = 20\,000 - 3200(5)$
$= \$4000$
Declining balance:
$S = 20\,000(0.76)^{5}$
$= \$5071.05$ to the nearest cent
The straight-line method gives the lower salvage value, $\$4000$.

options.why: Took $16\%$ of the purchase price; this is the first year's declining-balance loss, which decreases in later years, rather than the straight-line annual amount.
Read the purchase price off the vertical axis instead of the yearly loss.
Halved the purchase price instead of dividing it by the $9$-year life shown.

questions.solution_text:
The straight line starts at $\$18\,000$ and reaches $\$0$ after $9$ years.
$D = \dfrac{18\,000}{9}$
$= \$2000$ per year

questions.question_text:
A truck costing $\$95\,000$ is depreciated by $\$8000$ per year for $4$ years, after which the declining-balance method at $20\%$ p.a. is used.
What is its value $8$ years after purchase?

options.why: Used straight-line depreciation for all $8$ years and ignored the change of method.
Stopped at the changeover and gave the value at the end of year $4$.
Applied only one year of declining balance instead of the remaining four.
